title: The worker brief's always-in-scope rule tells a content worker to add a source row its touches may not cover, so done refuses _sources.csv
goal: The fixed brief rule of bl_dispatch.WORKER_RULES says a source row is in scope only in a file the item's touches name, or _sources.csv rows a content item adds count as in scope, so a worker that follows the brief is not refused at done; a research item whose touches name a kb root's articles has that root's _sources.csv in its touches, which the Plan rule of kb/_self/backlog.md and the kb-sprint skill's plan step 2 say; the _self rules answer 'may a research item add source rows outside its touches' with a good pack through a tested row of kb/_self/_retrieval/lookup_eval.csv

run: import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import bl_base,bl_dispatch;t=' '.join(str(r) for r in bl_dispatch.WORKER_RULES);sys.exit(0 if bl_base.in_scope('kb/public/_sources.csv',['kb/public/gitlab/foo.md']) or 'source row in a file the touches name' in t else 1)

import subprocess,sys;t=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'_tools/rag.py','pack','--root','_self','may a research item add source rows outside its touches'],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout;sys.exit(0 if t.startswith('coverage: good') else 1)

import sys;a=open('skills/sprint/SKILL.md',encoding='utf-8').read().split('## plan')[1].split('## start')[0];b=open('kb/_self/backlog.md',encoding='utf-8').read().splitlines();sys.exit(0 if '_sources.csv' in a and any('**Plan**' in l and '_sources.csv' in l for l in b) else 1)

gates.question: How does a content worker's source row count as in scope: the brief rule and planning put the root's _sources.csv in the item's touches, or kb/*/_sources.csv joins always_in_scope for every item?
options: the item's touches name the root's _sources.csv
gates.recommendation: the item's touches name the root's _sources.csv
gates.answer: the item's touches name the root's _sources.csv

notes: Found at the SP-q5ldd25k review: bl_base.always_in_scope holds the item files and the coverage files, not _sources.csv, yet the fixed brief rule tells a content worker a source row is in scope, so done refuses it. Absorbs ST-4q4zv34i (2026-10-13 triage): no code names _sources.csv (bl_plan, bl_base, bl_land, bl_dispatch); SP-4o3plg4l's research ST-z7eii5h6 stopped with three DOC facts and their source rows unlanded until its touches were widened and it was resumed (a second session, about 2.9 USD more); the pack for 'may a research item add source rows outside its touches' reads weak. Premise (planner, 2026-10-13): the repro exits 1 and python3 _tools/rag.py pack --root _self 'may a research item add source rows outside its touches' prints coverage: weak. Today new sprint files the goal research story with kb/public/**, which covers a root's _sources.csv; the plan rule matters when a planner narrows it to articles. Planned at the 2026-10-13 draft triage (sprint 11 of 15, "Worker runs are counted: work and usage rows reach cost, dispatch is safe in parallel, staged copies come back by tool"): it fixes a failure that recurred in recent sprints and blocks the EP-gzr4mmkm fitness test that a content sprint lands on headless Sonnet workers with no operator step beyond its gates.
